label: iteration-audit-current
runtime_source: Unchanged from the source revision. The temporary single-entity-lookup experiment was reverted and the release binaries rebuilt before these runs.
options: Each program's default full-size options, on one thread and on all twelve physical cores. Programs and repeats ran sequentially with no concurrent builds or benchmarks.
outcome: All end-state digests agreed. N-body failed to use the worker pool and took about 30 times as long as C with SIMD on twelve cores; events took about 13 times as long as C. These are the measurements before the scheduling fix.
followup_source: Same base and unchanged engine runtime; compiler/src/codegen.c distinguishes known constant loop trips from unknown nested loop work. A parallel step with unknown loop work uses the existing conservative scheduling fallback, restoring worker-pool selection. Includes compiler/tests/e2e/parallel_work.tide and parallel_work_test.c regression coverage.
followup_options: Same full suite, default counts and timing options, three sequential repetitions per concept, same CPU/compiler/flags, with no concurrent agent builds or benchmarks.
followup_outcome: All end-state digests agreed; the new scheduling regression passed. N-body selected the worker pool again and took about 4 times as long as C with SIMD on twelve cores, instead of about 30. Absolute timings varied during these runs (C timings changed too), so they do not establish exact cross-phase percentage improvements. Unknown nested loops can conservatively select the pool even when their actual workload is small.
